name: Pontypool mutual sickness benefits
description: A members’ friendly society provided financial assistance to a sick or injured member.

date.basis: Date of the specified episode, not a global origin claim.

events.statement: Isaac Williams, a member of the Sons of the Globe Society in Pontypool, received sick pay and a separate payment for broken bones.
events.scope: This documented community and episode; not a global first.

evidence.supports: The authors report the 1821 payments from society accounts.
The study explains voluntary-contribution mutual aid.

contributions.resource: Received society payments for sickness and injury.

evidence.supports: The authors report the 1821 payments from society accounts.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest scoped episode established in these sources, not universal priority.

caveats: One beneficiary does not establish all workers could join or all claims were paid; benefits and solvency varied.

research.note: Initial source pass; independent review remains open. Independent review checked Turner and Blackie pp. 112–113 and note 124: one recipient, four shillings weekly in 1821, plus a separate injury payment.

measures.money_context: Nominal 1821 British shillings; 20 shillings to one pound.
measures.subject: Isaac Williams’s reported sick pay
measures.conditions: One member case in 1821, not an average or standard payment.

evidence.supports: Reports four shillings weekly sick pay.
